steps.expected: The OBU accepts the MA and the associated mode profile (if any). Supervision is updated to the new MA.

test_cases.title: Replacement of route suitability loading gauge information
test_cases.preconditions: The OBU is in a mode where location based information is stored (e.g., Full Supervision). Existing route suitability loading gauge information is stored for a specific route section.
test_cases.test_inputs: New track description data containing route suitability loading gauge information for the same route section.

steps.action: Receive new track description data containing route suitability loading gauge information that overlaps with the stored information.
steps.expected: The OBU replaces all stored route suitability loading gauge information with the new information.

test_cases.title: Replacement of adhesion factor information from start location
test_cases.preconditions: The OBU has stored adhesion factor information for a track section starting at location L1 and ending at L2.
test_cases.test_inputs: New track description data containing adhesion factor information starting at location L3, where L1 < L3 < L2.

steps.action: Receive new track description data containing adhesion factor information starting at location L3.
steps.expected: The OBU replaces the stored adhesion factor information from location L3 onwards. The adhesion factor information between L1 and L3 remains unchanged.

test_cases.title: Replacement of linking information (non-infill) from reference balise group
test_cases.preconditions: The OBU has stored linking information with a reference balise group BG1.
test_cases.test_inputs: New linking information received as non-infill information with a reference balise group BG2.

steps.action: Receive new linking information as non-infill information with reference balise group BG2.
steps.expected: The OBU replaces all stored linking information from the reference balise group BG2 onwards.

test_cases.title: Replacement of linking information (infill) from infill reference location
test_cases.preconditions: The OBU has stored linking information.
test_cases.test_inputs: New linking information received as infill information with an infill reference location (balise group at next main signal) BG3.

steps.action: Receive new linking information as infill information with infill reference location BG3.
steps.expected: The OBU replaces all stored linking information from the infill reference location BG3 onwards.

test_cases.title: Resuming initial state for PBD speed restrictions on trackside request
test_cases.preconditions: The OBU has stored Speed Restriction to ensure Permitted Braking Distance (PBD) information beyond a given location L.
test_cases.test_inputs: Trackside request to resume initial state for PBD speed restrictions beyond location L.

steps.action: Receive a trackside request to resume initial state for stored Speed Restriction to ensure Permitted Braking Distance information beyond location L.
steps.expected: The OBU resumes the initial state for the PBD speed restriction information beyond location L.

test_cases.title: Resuming initial state for axle load speed profiles on trackside request
test_cases.preconditions: The OBU has stored axle load speed profile information beyond a given location L.
test_cases.test_inputs: Trackside request to resume initial state for axle load speed profiles beyond location L.

steps.action: Receive a trackside request to resume initial state for stored axle load speed profile information beyond location L.
steps.expected: The OBU resumes the initial state for the axle load speed profile information beyond location L.

test_cases.title: Resuming initial state for grouped track condition types on single request
test_cases.preconditions: The OBU has stored track condition information of types: sound horn, non stopping area, tunnel stopping area, powerless section – lower pantograph, powerless section – switch off the main power switch, radio hole, air tightness, switch off regenerative brake, switch off eddy current brake for service brake, switch off eddy current brake for emergency brake, and switch off magnetic shoe brake beyond a given location L.
test_cases.test_inputs: A single trackside request to resume initial state for the listed track condition types beyond location L.

steps.action: Receive a single trackside request to resume initial state for the grouped track condition types (sound horn, non stopping area, etc.) beyond location L.
steps.expected: The OBU resumes the initial state for all the listed track condition types beyond location L.

test_cases.title: Resuming initial state for route suitability data on single request
test_cases.preconditions: The OBU has stored route suitability information (loading gauge, traction system, axle load) beyond a given location L.
test_cases.test_inputs: A single trackside request to resume initial state for all stored route suitability information beyond location L.

steps.action: Receive a single trackside request to resume initial state for all stored route suitability information beyond location L.
steps.expected: The OBU resumes the initial state for all stored route suitability information beyond location L.

test_cases.title: Resuming initial state for Station Platform track conditions on single request
test_cases.preconditions: The OBU has stored track condition information of type Station Platform beyond a given location L.
test_cases.test_inputs: A single trackside request to resume initial state for all stored track condition information of the type Station Platform beyond location L.

steps.action: Receive a single trackside request to resume initial state for all stored track condition information of the type Station Platform beyond location L.
steps.expected: The OBU resumes the initial state for the Station Platform track condition information beyond location L.

test_cases.title: Supervised Manoeuvre with same validity direction as train orientation
test_cases.preconditions: The OBU is in a mode where location based information is stored. The current train orientation is forward. Location based information is stored for the forward direction.
test_cases.test_inputs: A Supervised Manoeuvre authorisation with a validity direction matching the current train orientation (forward).

steps.action: Receive a Supervised Manoeuvre authorisation with a validity direction matching the current train orientation.
steps.expected: The OBU applies the normal replacement rules of SUBSET-026 §3.7.3.1 to the location based information.

test_cases.title: Supervised Manoeuvre with opposite validity direction to train orientation
test_cases.preconditions: The OBU is in a mode where location based information is stored. The current train orientation is forward. Location based information is stored for the forward direction.
test_cases.test_inputs: A Supervised Manoeuvre authorisation with a validity direction opposite to the current train orientation (backward).

steps.action: Receive a Supervised Manoeuvre authorisation with a validity direction opposite to the current train orientation.
steps.expected: The OBU does not apply the normal replacement rules. Instead, it deletes all previously stored location based information.

test_cases.title: MA request includes all applicable reasons when multiple triggers occur simultaneously
test_cases.preconditions: Level 2, communication session established with RBC. MA request parameters received from RBC. Train is in Full Supervision (FS) mode with a valid Movement Authority (MA). The train is approaching a perturbation location such that the time-before-reaching criterion is met. Simultaneously, a Section timer for the current MA is running and the time-before-expiration criterion for that timer is also met.
test_cases.assumptions: The RBC is configured to accept MA requests with multiple reasons. The specific time values for the perturbation and timer criteria are set such that both conditions are true at the same instant.

steps.action: Allow the train to reach the point where the time-before-reaching the perturbation location criterion is fulfilled AND the time-before-Section-timer-expiration criterion is fulfilled simultaneously.
steps.expected: The OBU sends an MA request to the RBC. The request message contains both reasons: 'Time before reaching the perturbation location reached' and 'Time before a Section timer/LOA speed timer expires reached'.

test_cases.title: MA request includes 'Start' reason and timer reason when driver selects Start while timer criterion is met
test_cases.preconditions: Level 2, communication session established with RBC. MA request parameters received. Train is at standstill or moving slowly. A Section timer is running and the time-before-expiration criterion is met. The driver has not yet selected 'Start' for this MA cycle.
test_cases.assumptions: The 'Start' selection is a valid trigger for MA request in Level 2.

steps.action: While the time-before-Section-timer-expiration criterion is met, the driver selects 'Start' on the DMI.
steps.expected: The OBU sends an MA request to the RBC. The request message contains both reasons: 'Start selected by driver' and 'Time before a Section timer/LOA speed timer expires reached'.

test_cases.title: MA request triggered when train front passes perturbation location criterion
test_cases.preconditions: Level 2, communication session established with RBC. MA request parameters received from RBC defining the time-before-reaching criterion for perturbation location. Train is in FS mode with a valid MA containing a perturbation location. The train is running at a speed such that the calculated trigger location is ahead of the train front.
test_cases.assumptions: The perturbation location is defined in the current MA. The train speed is constant and known to the OBU.

steps.action: Allow the train to run until the train front passes the location calculated by the OBU based on the 'time before reaching the perturbation location' criterion.
steps.expected: The OBU triggers and sends an MA request to the RBC with the reason 'Time before reaching the perturbation location reached'.

test_cases.title: MA request triggered when Section timer expiration criterion is reached
test_cases.preconditions: Level 2, communication session established with RBC. MA request parameters received from RBC defining the time-before-expiration criterion for Section timers. Train is in FS mode with a valid MA that includes a Section timer. The Section timer is running.
test_cases.assumptions: The Section timer value is set such that the 'time before expiration' threshold is reached before the timer itself expires.

steps.action: Wait until the time remaining on the Section timer equals the defined 'time before expiration' value specified in the MA request parameters.
steps.expected: The OBU triggers and sends an MA request to the RBC with the reason 'Time before a Section timer/LOA speed timer expires reached'.

test_cases.title: MA request triggered when LOA speed timer expiration criterion is reached
test_cases.preconditions: Level 2, communication session established with RBC. MA request parameters received from RBC defining the time-before-expiration criterion for LOA speed timers. Train is in FS mode with a valid MA that includes a LOA speed timer. The LOA speed timer is running.
test_cases.assumptions: The LOA speed timer is active and running.

steps.action: Wait until the time remaining on the LOA speed timer equals the defined 'time before expiration' value specified in the MA request parameters.
steps.expected: The OBU triggers and sends an MA request to the RBC with the reason 'Time before a Section timer/LOA speed timer expires reached'.

test_cases.title: MA request sent upon track description deletion (valid situation)
test_cases.preconditions: Level 2, communication session established with RBC. Train is in FS mode with a valid MA. The OBU has stored track description data (e.g., speed restrictions or route suitability) that is subject to deletion under a situation defined in SUBSET-026 Appendix A.3.4, excluding situations a, b, f, and k (e.g., situation c: deletion due to new MA reception or similar valid trigger).
test_cases.assumptions: The specific deletion situation is one of the valid ones listed in A.3.4 (not a, b, f, k).

steps.action: Trigger a condition that causes the OBU to delete a part of the stored track description according to a valid situation in SUBSET-026 Appendix A.3.4 (e.g., reception of a new MA that overrides previous track description elements).
steps.expected: The OBU sends an MA request to the RBC with the reason 'Track description deletion'.

test_cases.title: No MA request sent upon track description deletion (excluded situation a)
test_cases.preconditions: Level 2, communication session established with RBC. Train is in FS mode with a valid MA. The OBU has stored track description data. A condition occurs that corresponds to situation 'a' in SUBSET-026 Appendix A.3.4, which is explicitly excluded from triggering an MA request.
test_cases.assumptions: Situation 'a' in A.3.4 is a defined exclusion case (e.g., deletion of data that does not affect the current MA supervision or is routine housekeeping).

steps.action: Trigger a condition that causes the OBU to delete a part of the stored track description according to situation 'a' in SUBSET-026 Appendix A.3.4.
steps.expected: The OBU does NOT send an MA request to the RBC with the reason 'Track description deletion'.

test_cases.title: End Section timer start upon passing start location
test_cases.preconditions: Train is in a mode where MA is active (e.g., FS). An MA with an End Section timer start location is stored. The train's max safe front end is located before the End Section timer start location.

steps.action: Move the train forward until its max safe front end passes the End Section timer start location.
steps.expected: The End Section timer starts counting.

test_cases.title: End Section timer timeout consequences
test_cases.preconditions: End Section timer is running. The MA includes an LOA with a non-zero target speed at the End of Movement Authority. Location based information per Appendix A.3.4 is stored.

test_cases.title: LOA speed timer start in Level 2
test_cases.preconditions: Level 2 operation. Communication session with RBC is established. Train is in FS mode.

steps.action: Receive a new MA message from the RBC containing a LOA speed.
steps.expected: The LOA speed timer starts at the time stamp of the received message.

test_cases.title: LOA speed timer start in Level 1
test_cases.preconditions: Level 1 operation. Train is in FS mode. A balise group giving an MA with a LOA speed is ahead.

steps.action: Pass the first encountered balise of the balise group giving the MA.
steps.expected: The LOA speed timer starts at the moment of passing the first balise.

test_cases.title: LOA speed timer timeout consequences
test_cases.preconditions: LOA speed timer is running. The MA includes an LOA with a non-zero target speed. Location based information per Appendix A.3.4 is stored.

steps.action: Wait until the LOA speed timer value exceeds the time-out value received from trackside.
steps.expected: The speed associated with the LOA is set to zero. The LOA becomes an EOA. The Supervised Location is defined per §3.8.4.5. The location based information listed in Appendix A.3.4 is deleted.

test_cases.title: Overlap timer start upon passing start location
test_cases.preconditions: Train is in a mode where MA is active. An MA with an Overlap timer start location and a finite time-out value is stored. The train's max safe front end is located before the Overlap timer start location.

steps.action: Move the train forward until its max safe front end passes the Overlap timer start location.
steps.expected: The Overlap timer starts counting.

test_cases.title: Overlap timer start with infinite time-out value
test_cases.preconditions: Train is in a mode where MA is active. An MA with an Overlap timer start location and a time-out value of 'infinite' is stored. The train's max safe front end is located before the Overlap timer start location.

steps.action: Move the train forward until its max safe front end passes the Overlap timer start location.
steps.expected: The Overlap timer is considered as started.

test_cases.title: Overlap timer timeout consequences
test_cases.preconditions: Overlap timer is running. The MA includes an Overlap with a release speed and a non-zero target speed at the End of Movement Authority. Location based information per Appendix A.3.4 is stored.

steps.action: Wait until the Overlap timer value exceeds the time-out value given by trackside.
steps.expected: The overlap information is deleted. The release speed associated with the Overlap is deleted. The Supervised Location is redetermined per §3.8.4.5. The location based information listed in Appendix A.3.4 is deleted. The non-zero target speed at the End of Movement Authority is set to zero.

test_cases.title: Overlap timer expiration upon train standstill
test_cases.preconditions: Overlap timer is running. The train is moving.

steps.action: Bring the train to a standstill while the Overlap timer is running.
steps.expected: The OBU treats the Overlap timer as expired. The consequences defined for Overlap time-out (deletion of overlap, release speed, redetermination of SvL, setting target speed to zero) are applied.

test_cases.title: Overlap timer expiration upon receiving new MA with rear start location
test_cases.preconditions: No Overlap timer is running. The train's max safe front end is at a specific position.

steps.expected: The OBU considers that the Overlap timer has exceeded its time-out value. The consequences defined for Overlap time-out (deletion of overlap, release speed, redetermination of SvL, setting target speed to zero) are applied.

test_cases.title: Supervised Location determination with valid Overlap
test_cases.preconditions: An MA with an Overlap is stored. The Overlap timer is running and has not timed out. A Danger Point and an End Section are also defined in the MA.

test_cases.title: Supervised Location determination with no Overlap and no Danger Point

steps.action: Check the Supervised Location (SvL) determined by the OBU.

test_cases.title: Non-infill MA from RBC replaces all previous MA data
test_cases.preconditions: Level 2, train in FS, OS, LS or AD. An MA with specific data (e.g., gradient profile, speed restrictions) is currently stored and supervised.

test_cases.title: Non-infill MA from main-signal balise group replaces all previous MA data
test_cases.preconditions: Level 1, train in FS, LS or AD. An MA is currently stored. The train is approaching a main signal balise group.
test_cases.test_inputs: A balise group message at the main signal containing a non-infill MA with different data.

test_cases.title: Boundary case: Train front end exactly at the Indication supervision limit
test_cases.preconditions: Level 2, communication session with RBC established, train running in a mode with valid MA. The train front end position is estimated to be exactly at the Indication supervision limit of the proposed shortened MA.
test_cases.test_inputs: RBC sends a 'Request to shorten MA' message containing a proposed shortened MA with an EOA closer to the train than the current EOA.
test_cases.assumptions: The requirement states 'in rear' for acceptance and 'in advance' for rejection. The behavior at the exact limit is not explicitly defined in the provided text, but typically 'in rear' implies strictly behind. However, in safety-critical systems, if the limit is the boundary of the supervision area, being exactly at it might be considered 'in rear' or 'in advance' depending on implementation. Assuming 'in rear' means position < limit and 'in advance' means position >= limit, or vice versa. Let's assume the standard interpretation where if the train has not passed the limit, it is in rear. If the train is exactly at the limit, it has not passed it, so it should be accepted. If the requirement implies strict inequality, this test verifies the boundary. Let's assume acceptance if position <= limit (in rear or at) and rejection if position > limit (in advance).

steps.action: The RBC sends a request to shorten the MA such that the Indication supervision limit is exactly at the current estimated train front end position.
steps.expected: The OBU evaluates the position. Assuming 'in rear' includes the limit position (or the limit is the start of the new MA's supervision), the OBU accepts the request, adopts the new MA, and informs the RBC of acceptance.

test_cases.title: Sound horn indication start uses estimated front end

test_cases.title: Text message appearance for auxiliary information without acknowledgement

test_cases.title: Start condition with multiple sub-conditions defined as 'any'
test_cases.preconditions: OBU is in a mode where text messages can be displayed. Train is moving.
test_cases.test_inputs: A text message with start condition defined by two sub-conditions (e.g., 'location' and 'speed') with the logic 'any' (OR). The train is not at the location but is at the required speed.

steps.action: Receive a text message where the start condition requires either 'location A' OR 'speed > 50 km/h'. The train is at speed 60 km/h but not at location A.
steps.expected: The OBU considers the start condition fulfilled because one of the sub-conditions (speed) is met, and the text message is displayed.

test_cases.title: Start condition with multiple sub-conditions defined as 'all'
test_cases.preconditions: OBU is in a mode where text messages can be displayed. Train is moving.
test_cases.test_inputs: A text message with start condition defined by two sub-conditions (e.g., 'location' and 'speed') with the logic 'all' (AND). The train is at the location but not at the required speed.

steps.action: Receive a text message where the start condition requires both 'location A' AND 'speed > 50 km/h'. The train is at location A but speed is 30 km/h.
steps.expected: The OBU does not consider the start condition fulfilled because not all sub-conditions are met. The text message is not displayed.

steps.action: The train accelerates to 60 km/h while remaining at location A.
steps.expected: The OBU considers the start condition fulfilled because both sub-conditions are now met, and the text message is displayed.

test_cases.title: Start condition with no sub-conditions defined
test_cases.preconditions: OBU is in a mode where text messages can be displayed.
test_cases.test_inputs: A text message with no start sub-conditions defined.

steps.action: Receive a text message from trackside that defines no start sub-conditions.
steps.expected: The OBU treats the start condition as immediately fulfilled and displays the text message (provided the end condition is not also immediately fulfilled).

test_cases.title: Driver acknowledgement ends display regardless of end condition
test_cases.preconditions: OBU is displaying a text message that requests driver acknowledgement. The end condition is defined as 'location B' which has not been reached yet.
test_cases.test_inputs: A text message with driver acknowledgement requested, configured such that acknowledgement always ends the display.

steps.action: The driver acknowledges the text message before reaching location B.
steps.expected: The OBU stops displaying the text message immediately upon acknowledgement, even though the end condition (location B) has not been fulfilled.

test_cases.title: Driver acknowledgement is a necessary condition for ending display
test_cases.preconditions: OBU is displaying a text message that requests driver acknowledgement. The end condition is defined as 'location B'.
test_cases.test_inputs: A text message with driver acknowledgement requested, configured such that acknowledgement is a necessary condition in addition to the end condition.

steps.action: The train reaches location B (end condition fulfilled) but the driver has not acknowledged the message.
steps.expected: The OBU continues to display the text message because the driver acknowledgement is still required.

steps.action: The driver acknowledges the text message after the train has passed location B.
steps.expected: The OBU stops displaying the text message upon acknowledgement, as both the end condition and the acknowledgement are now fulfilled.

test_cases.title: No display if end condition is immediately fulfilled
test_cases.preconditions: OBU is in a mode where text messages can be displayed.
test_cases.test_inputs: A text message with start condition 'immediately fulfilled' (no sub-conditions) and end condition 'location A' where the train is currently at location A.

steps.action: Receive a text message where the start condition is immediately fulfilled and the end condition (location A) is also already fulfilled at the moment of receipt.
steps.expected: The OBU does not display the text message at all, even if driver confirmation is requested.

test_cases.title: Display length measured from start location
test_cases.preconditions: OBU is in a mode where text messages can be displayed. Train is moving.

steps.action: The train travels 1000m from location A and reaches location B.
steps.expected: The text message is no longer displayed, as the end condition (location B) is fulfilled. The display length was measured from the start location A.

test_cases.title: Temporary EOA and SvL: Mode Profile requires SvL at start
test_cases.preconditions: OBU is in Full Supervision (FS) mode. A new MA with a Mode Profile (e.g., OS or LS) is received. The Mode Profile requires a temporary SvL at its start location. The OBU has not yet switched to the Mode Profile's mode.

test_cases.title: Replacement of stored Level Crossing information with new information of the same identity
test_cases.preconditions: The OBU is in a mode where Level Crossing information is processed (e.g., FS, OS, LS, or AD). A Level Crossing (LX) information set with a specific identity (e.g., LX_ID_1) is already stored in the OBU memory. The train is approaching the location of this stored LX.
test_cases.test_inputs: A new Level Crossing information message with the same identity (LX_ID_1) but different parameters (e.g., different protection status or length) is transmitted to the OBU (via balise or radio, depending on the level).
test_cases.assumptions: The new LX information is valid and accepted by the OBU according to other acceptance criteria (e.g., timing, format).

steps.action: Verify the stored Level Crossing information in the OBU before receiving the new message.
steps.expected: The OBU holds the initial Level Crossing information with identity LX_ID_1 and its original parameters (e.g., protected status, start location, length).

steps.action: Transmit the new Level Crossing information with the same identity (LX_ID_1) to the OBU.
steps.expected: The OBU receives the new Level Crossing information.

steps.action: Inspect the Level Crossing information stored in the OBU after the reception.
steps.expected: The stored Level Crossing information for identity LX_ID_1 is replaced by the new information. The old parameters are no longer present, and the new parameters (e.g., updated protection status or length) are active.

test_cases.title: Independence of Level Crossing information with different identities
test_cases.preconditions: The OBU is in a mode where Level Crossing information is processed. Two distinct Level Crossing information sets with different identities (LX_ID_A and LX_ID_B) are stored in the OBU memory.

steps.action: Verify the stored Level Crossing information for both identities (LX_ID_A and LX_ID_B) before the update.
steps.expected: Both LX_ID_A and LX_ID_B are stored with their respective initial parameters.

steps.action: Transmit the new Level Crossing information with identity LX_ID_A to the OBU.
steps.expected: The OBU receives the new Level Crossing information for LX_ID_A.

steps.action: Inspect the Level Crossing information stored in the OBU for both identities after the reception.
steps.expected: The stored information for LX_ID_A is replaced by the new data. The stored information for LX_ID_B remains unchanged, confirming that the replacement is specific to the identity and does not affect other LX information.

test_cases.preconditions: An active company representative account exists at AAL2 with a phishing-resistant authenticator (e.g., passkey) bound to it. A test environment simulating an impostor verifier (phishing site) is available.

test_cases.title: Inactivity timeout terminates AAL2 session
test_cases.preconditions: A citizen or company representative is authenticated in an AAL2 session. The inactivity timeout value is defined in VBP SDD §14 (assumed to be 1 hour for testing).
test_cases.assumptions: The inactivity timeout is set to a short duration (e.g., 1 minute) in the test environment to facilitate testing, or the system clock can be manipulated.

steps.action: Perform an action within the session (e.g., navigate to a page) to ensure the session is active.
steps.expected: The session remains active and the inactivity timer is reset.

steps.action: Wait for the inactivity timeout period to elapse without performing any actions.
steps.expected: The session is terminated. The user is redirected to the login page or receives a session expired message.

steps.action: Attempt to access a protected resource directly via URL or API call.
steps.expected: Access is denied, and the user is prompted to reauthenticate.

test_cases.title: Overall timeout terminates AAL2 session
test_cases.preconditions: A citizen or company representative is authenticated in an AAL2 session. The overall timeout value is defined in VBP SDD §14 (assumed to be 24 hours for testing).
test_cases.assumptions: The overall timeout is set to a short duration (e.g., 2 minutes) in the test environment to facilitate testing, or the system clock can be manipulated.

steps.action: Perform periodic actions within the session to keep the inactivity timer reset, but do not reauthenticate.
steps.expected: The session remains active as long as the inactivity timeout is not exceeded.

steps.action: Wait for the overall timeout period to elapse from the initial authentication or last reauthentication.
steps.expected: The session is terminated regardless of recent activity. The user is redirected to the login page.

steps.action: Attempt to access a protected resource directly via URL or API call.
steps.expected: Access is denied, and the user is prompted to reauthenticate.

test_cases.title: Session activity resets inactivity timeout
test_cases.preconditions: A citizen or company representative is authenticated in an AAL2 session. The inactivity timeout is set to a short duration (e.g., 2 minutes).

steps.expected: The session is still active.

steps.action: Perform an action within the session (e.g., click a button or navigate).
steps.expected: The inactivity timer is reset.

steps.action: Wait for the full inactivity timeout period (e.g., 2 minutes) from the last action.
steps.expected: The session is terminated.

test_cases.title: Successful reauthentication resets both timeouts
test_cases.preconditions: A citizen or company representative is authenticated in an AAL2 session. The inactivity and overall timeouts are set to short durations for testing.

steps.action: Wait for a period close to the inactivity timeout, then trigger the reauthentication prompt (if available) or wait for the session to expire and reauthenticate.
steps.expected: The user is prompted to reauthenticate or the session expires.

steps.action: Complete the reauthentication process successfully.
steps.expected: A new session is established. Both the inactivity and overall timers are reset.

steps.action: Wait for the original inactivity timeout period from the initial authentication (not the reauthentication).
steps.expected: The session is still active because the timer was reset by reauthentication.

test_cases.title: Reauthentication using password/biometric with session secret after inactivity timeout
test_cases.preconditions: A citizen or company representative is authenticated in an AAL2 session. The inactivity timeout has occurred, but the overall timeout has not yet occurred. The system supports reauthentication using a password or biometric in conjunction with the session secret.
test_cases.assumptions: The system is configured to allow simplified reauthentication (password/biometric + session secret) after inactivity timeout but before overall timeout, as per NIST SP 800-63B-4 §5.2.

steps.action: Wait for the inactivity timeout to elapse.
steps.expected: The session is marked as inactive or terminated, but the overall session context is still valid.

steps.action: Attempt to access a protected resource.
steps.expected: The user is prompted to reauthenticate. The prompt allows reauthentication using only a password or biometric (in conjunction with the session secret), not full multi-factor authentication.

test_cases.title: Changing the pre-registered telephone number requires the full binding process

steps.expected: The system rejects the request or redirects to the authenticator binding process, ensuring the change is treated as binding a new authenticator.

test_cases.title: Binding an AAL2 authenticator to an AAL2 account requires AAL2 authentication

steps.action: Initiate the binding of the new AAL2 authenticator while authenticated only at AAL1 (e.g., password only, if the system allows partial sessions, or simulate a state where the current session strength is AAL1).

test_cases.title: Geçerli e-Devlet imzası ile oturum açma
test_cases.preconditions: VBP, e-Devlet test ortamına entegre edilmiştir. e-Devlet test IdP'si, VBP'nin doğrulama anahtarına sahip geçerli imzalı assertion'lar üretebilmektedir. Test vatandaş kimliği mevcuttur.

steps.action: Test vatandaş kimliğiyle e-Devlet üzerinden giriş başlatılır ve e-Devlet tarafından imzalanmış, VBP'ye gönderilen assertion VBP'ye iletilir.
steps.expected: VBP, assertion'ın imzasını e-Devlet'e ait doğrulama anahtarıyla doğrular ve oturumu başarıyla açar.

test_cases.title: Geçersiz imzalı assertion'ın reddedilmesi
test_cases.preconditions: VBP, e-Devlet test ortamına entegre edilmiştir. VBP'nin federation endpoint'ine doğrudan assertion gönderilebilecek bir araç (örneğin intercepting proxy veya test istemcisi) mevcuttur.
test_cases.assumptions: Assertion içeriği (audience, nonce, issuer vb.) geçerli olsa da imza, e-Devlet'in doğrulama anahtarına karşılık gelmeyen farklı bir anahtarla imzalanmıştır.

steps.action: İçeriği geçerli ancak imzası e-Devlet'e ait olmayan (farklı bir anahtarla imzalanmış) bir assertion VBP'ye gönderilir.
steps.expected: VBP, imza doğrulamasını başarısız olur, assertion'ı reddeder ve oturum açılmaz.

test_cases.title: Bozuk veya eksik imzalı assertion'ın reddedilmesi
test_cases.preconditions: VBP, e-Devlet test ortamına entegre edilmiştir. VBP'nin federation endpoint'ine doğrudan assertion gönderilebilecek bir araç mevcuttur.
test_cases.assumptions: Assertion'ın imza alanı bozulmuş, eksik veya formatı hatalıdır.

steps.action: İmza alanı bozulmuş veya eksik bir assertion VBP'ye gönderilir.
steps.expected: VBP, imza doğrulamasını başarısız olur, assertion'ı reddeder ve oturum açılmaz.

test_cases.title: Acceptance of a valid e-Devlet assertion on first presentation
test_cases.preconditions: A test e-Devlet IdP or test double is configured to issue valid assertions for VBP. A test citizen identity is available. An intercepting proxy or test harness is available to capture and replay the assertion.

steps.action: Initiate a sign-in flow as a test citizen through the e-Devlet test IdP.
steps.expected: The e-Devlet IdP issues a valid assertion and redirects to VBP's callback URL.

steps.action: Allow VBP to process the assertion for the first time.
steps.expected: VBP accepts the assertion, validates it, and establishes a citizen session.

test_cases.title: Rejection of a replayed e-Devlet assertion
test_cases.preconditions: A valid e-Devlet assertion has already been successfully presented to VBP and a session was established. The same assertion is captured and available for replay.

steps.action: Present the exact same e-Devlet assertion that was previously accepted to VBP's callback endpoint again.
steps.expected: VBP rejects the assertion due to replay protection and does not establish a new session or extend the existing one.

steps.action: Verify the system logs or error response for the rejected request.
steps.expected: The rejection is logged or indicated as a replay attack or invalid assertion state.

test_cases.title: VBP initiates the federation transaction as the RP
test_cases.preconditions: VBP is configured with a valid e-Devlet test IdP endpoint. A test citizen account exists in the e-Devlet test environment. An intercepting proxy or browser developer tools are available to capture network traffic.

steps.action: Initiate a citizen login on the VBP portal by clicking the 'Login with e-Devlet' button.
steps.expected: VBP generates an authorization request and redirects the user's browser to the e-Devlet IdP endpoint. The request is initiated by VBP (the RP), not by the IdP.

steps.action: Inspect the captured authorization request sent from VBP to e-Devlet.
steps.expected: The request contains VBP's client identifier (RP identifier) and a cryptographic nonce, confirming that VBP is the initiating party of the federation transaction.

test_cases.title: Unsuccessful applicant receives generic error message
test_cases.preconditions: A test environment with mock authoritative sources configured to return mismatched data for a specific test applicant profile.
test_cases.test_inputs: Applicant data with self-asserted information that does not match the authoritative source data.

steps.action: Submit a company representative proofing application with self-asserted information that is known to be incorrect (mismatched with the authoritative source).
steps.expected: The system rejects the application and displays a generic error message indicating that the identity proofing was unsuccessful, without specifying which field or attribute failed verification.

steps.action: Submit a second company representative proofing application with self-asserted information that is known to be correct (matched with the authoritative source).
steps.expected: The system accepts the application and proceeds to the next step or confirms success, displaying a success message that does not reveal the specific validation logic or source details.

test_cases.title: Error messages do not reveal specific attribute mismatches
test_cases.preconditions: A test environment with mock authoritative sources configured to return mismatched data for specific attributes (e.g., name, date of birth, ID number).
test_cases.test_inputs: Applicant data with a single attribute mismatched (e.g., incorrect date of birth) and another with a different single attribute mismatched (e.g., incorrect ID number).

steps.action: Submit a proofing application where only the date of birth is incorrect.
steps.expected: The system returns a generic failure message. The message does not indicate that the date of birth was the specific cause of failure.

steps.action: Submit a proofing application where only the ID number is incorrect.
steps.expected: The system returns the same generic failure message as in the previous step. The message does not indicate that the ID number was the specific cause of failure.

steps.action: Compare the error messages from the two failed attempts.
steps.expected: The error messages are identical or indistinguishable in terms of revealing which specific attribute failed validation.

test_cases.title: Timing analysis does not reveal validation success or failure
test_cases.preconditions: A test environment with mock authoritative sources configured to return mismatched and matched data. A tool to measure response times is available.
test_cases.test_inputs: Multiple sets of applicant data, some with correct information and some with incorrect information.
test_cases.assumptions: The system's response time variance due to network latency is negligible or controlled for in the test environment.

steps.action: Submit a proofing application with correct self-asserted information and record the response time.
steps.expected: The system processes the request and returns a success response. The response time is recorded.

steps.action: Submit a proofing application with incorrect self-asserted information and record the response time.
steps.expected: The system processes the request and returns a failure response. The response time is recorded.

steps.action: Repeat steps 1 and 2 multiple times to gather statistical data on response times for successful and failed validations.
steps.expected: The average response times for successful and failed validations are statistically indistinguishable, preventing an attacker from inferring the outcome based on timing differences.

test_cases.title: Validation of core attributes against an authoritative source
test_cases.preconditions: A test applicant with valid core attributes (government identifier, name, date of birth) that match the records in the authoritative source (e.g., e-Devlet or Nüfus ve Vatandaşlık İşleri test database).
test_cases.test_inputs: Applicant details matching the authoritative source.

steps.action: Initiate IAL2 identity proofing for a company representative and provide core attributes that match the authoritative source.
steps.expected: The system validates the attributes successfully against the authoritative source.

steps.action: Complete the proofing process.
steps.expected: The proofing is accepted and the account is created or updated with the validated attributes.

test_cases.title: Validation of digitally signed attributes on SUPERIOR evidence
test_cases.preconditions: A test applicant with a valid SUPERIOR evidence document (e.g., e-Devlet identity or digital ID) containing digitally signed core attributes and a valid trust chain to a trust anchor.
test_cases.test_inputs: SUPERIOR evidence with valid digital signatures.

steps.action: Initiate IAL2 identity proofing and present SUPERIOR evidence with digitally signed core attributes.
steps.expected: The system validates the digital signatures and the trust chain using the issuer's public key.

steps.action: Complete the proofing process.
steps.expected: The proofing is accepted and the account is created or updated with the validated attributes.

test_cases.title: Rejection of mismatched core attributes against authoritative source
test_cases.preconditions: A test applicant with core attributes that do not match the authoritative source (e.g., incorrect date of birth or name).
test_cases.test_inputs: Applicant details mismatching the authoritative source.

steps.action: Initiate IAL2 identity proofing and provide core attributes that do not match the authoritative source.
steps.expected: The system fails to validate the attributes against the authoritative source.

steps.action: Attempt to complete the proofing process.
steps.expected: The proofing is rejected and an error message indicating attribute mismatch is displayed.

test_cases.title: Rejection of SUPERIOR evidence with invalid digital signature
test_cases.preconditions: A test applicant with SUPERIOR evidence that has an invalid or tampered digital signature.
test_cases.test_inputs: SUPERIOR evidence with invalid digital signature.

steps.action: Initiate IAL2 identity proofing and present SUPERIOR evidence with an invalid digital signature.
steps.expected: The system fails to validate the digital signature.

steps.action: Attempt to complete the proofing process.
steps.expected: The proofing is rejected and an error message indicating invalid evidence is displayed.

test_cases.title: Notification of proofing sent to validated address with required content
test_cases.preconditions: A company representative account is in the state immediately after successful IAL2 identity proofing. The applicant has a validated postal address or phone number on file. The notification service is configured to log outgoing messages.
test_cases.assumptions: The system uses a test double for the postal/phone delivery mechanism that captures the message content for inspection.

steps.action: Complete the IAL2 identity proofing process for a company representative with a validated postal address.
steps.expected: The system triggers the notification of proofing process.

steps.action: Inspect the captured notification message sent to the validated postal address.
steps.expected: The notification is addressed to the validated postal address.

steps.action: Verify the content of the notification message.
steps.expected: The message includes the name of the identity service and the date on which the identity proofing was completed.

steps.action: Verify the dispute instructions in the notification message.
steps.expected: The message provides clear instructions and contact information for the recipient to take if they repudiate their participation in the identity proofing event.

steps.action: Verify the security and confidentiality information in the notification message.
steps.expected: The message provides information about how the organization or CSP protects the security and confidentiality of the information it collects.

steps.action: Verify the subscriber responsibilities information in the notification message.
steps.expected: The message provides information about any responsibilities that the recipient has as a subscriber of the identity service.

test_cases.title: Notification of proofing sent to validated phone number
test_cases.preconditions: A company representative account is in the state immediately after successful IAL2 identity proofing. The applicant has a validated phone number on file but no validated postal address. The notification service is configured to log outgoing messages.
test_cases.assumptions: The system uses a test double for the SMS/phone delivery mechanism that captures the message content for inspection.

steps.action: Complete the IAL2 identity proofing process for a company representative with a validated phone number.
steps.expected: The system triggers the notification of proofing process.

steps.action: Inspect the captured notification message sent to the validated phone number.
steps.expected: The notification is delivered to the validated phone number.

steps.action: Verify the content of the notification message.
steps.expected: The message includes the name of the identity service, the date of proofing, dispute instructions, security/confidentiality info, and subscriber responsibilities as required by NIST SP 800-63A-4 §3.10.

test_cases.title: Notification not sent if no validated address exists
test_cases.preconditions: A company representative account is in the state immediately after successful IAL2 identity proofing. The applicant has no validated postal address, phone number, or email address on file. The notification service is configured to log outgoing messages.
test_cases.assumptions: The system is expected to handle the absence of a validated address gracefully, either by logging an error or skipping the notification without crashing the proofing process.

steps.action: Complete the IAL2 identity proofing process for a company representative with no validated address on file.
steps.expected: The proofing process completes successfully.

steps.action: Check the notification service logs for any outgoing messages.
steps.expected: No notification of proofing is sent to any address, as no validated address exists. The system may log an error or warning indicating the missing validated address.

test_cases.title: Knowledge-based verification is not used during company representative proofing
test_cases.preconditions: A test environment with a company representative proofing flow accessible. The flow is configured to require identity verification.
test_cases.test_inputs: Valid company representative identity evidence (e.g., T.C. Kimlik Kartı) and biometric sample (e.g., facial image).
test_cases.assumptions: The proofing flow is designed to use biometric or document-based verification methods as per NIST SP 800-63A-4.

steps.action: Initiate the company representative proofing process and proceed to the identity verification step.
steps.expected: The system does not present any knowledge-based verification questions (e.g., 'What is your mother's maiden name?', 'What was your first car?') as a method to verify identity.

steps.action: Complete the identity verification using the supported non-KBV method (e.g., biometric match or document validation).
steps.expected: The verification succeeds without any prompt for knowledge-based answers.

test_cases.title: Email is not offered as an out-of-band authentication method
test_cases.preconditions: A registered user account with the ability to configure or select authentication methods.

steps.action: Navigate to the security or authentication settings page for the user account.
steps.expected: The list of available out-of-band authentication methods does not include 'Email' or 'Email Code'.

steps.action: Initiate a sign-in or re-authentication flow that requires out-of-band verification.
steps.expected: The system does not present an option to receive the authentication code via email.

test_cases.title: Email-based out-of-band authentication request is rejected
test_cases.preconditions: A user account exists. The system's API or internal logic is accessible for testing (e.g., via a test harness or API client).
test_cases.test_inputs: A request to initiate out-of-band authentication specifying 'email' as the channel.
test_cases.assumptions: The system exposes an interface or internal function that allows specifying the out-of-band channel type for testing purposes.

steps.action: Send a request to initiate out-of-band authentication with the channel type set to 'email'.
steps.expected: The system rejects the request with an error indicating that email is not a supported or allowed out-of-band authentication channel.

test_cases.title: SMS one-time code accepted only once during validity period
test_cases.preconditions: An active company representative account with SMS bound as a second factor to a verified test telephone number. The tester has access to the test telephone number to receive the SMS code.

steps.action: Initiate an authentication transaction for the company representative and request an SMS one-time code.
steps.expected: VBP sends an SMS one-time code to the registered test telephone number.

steps.action: Submit the received SMS one-time code in the first authentication transaction.
steps.expected: VBP accepts the code and completes the authentication successfully.

steps.action: Initiate a second authentication transaction for the same account and submit the same SMS one-time code while it is still within its validity period.
steps.expected: VBP rejects the code as invalid or already used.

test_cases.title: Generating a new SMS code does not reset the failed authentication count
test_cases.preconditions: An active company representative account with SMS bound as the second factor. The account has a non-zero failed authentication count (e.g., 1 failed attempt recorded).
test_cases.assumptions: The tester has access to the system logs or an administrative interface to verify the current failed authentication count.

steps.action: Record the current failed authentication count for the account.
steps.expected: The count is greater than 0.

steps.action: Initiate a sign-in attempt and request a new SMS one-time code.
steps.expected: A new SMS code is sent to the registered telephone number.

steps.action: Check the failed authentication count for the account.
steps.expected: The failed authentication count remains unchanged from the value recorded in step 1.

test_cases.title: Password with only lowercase letters is accepted

test_cases.test_inputs: A password of at least 15 characters consisting solely of lowercase ASCII letters, not present in the blocklist.

steps.action: Submit a password consisting only of lowercase letters (e.g., 15 'a's or a random lowercase string) that is not on the blocklist.
steps.expected: The password is accepted and stored without any error regarding character composition.

test_cases.title: Password with only digits is accepted

steps.action: Submit a password consisting only of digits (e.g., 15 '1's or a random numeric string) that is not on the blocklist.
steps.expected: The password is accepted and stored without any error regarding character composition.

test_cases.title: Password with only special characters is accepted

steps.action: Submit a password consisting only of special characters that is not on the blocklist.
steps.expected: The password is accepted and stored without any error regarding character composition.

test_cases.title: Password with only spaces is accepted

test_cases.test_inputs: A password of at least 15 characters consisting solely of space characters, not present in the blocklist.

steps.action: Submit a password consisting only of space characters (15 or more) that is not on the blocklist.
steps.expected: The password is accepted and stored without any error regarding character composition.

test_cases.title: Password length validation with Unicode characters
test_cases.preconditions: A company representative account is in a state where a password can be set (activation or change). The candidate password consists of 15 distinct Unicode characters (e.g., emojis or accented letters) that are not on the blocklist.

test_cases.assumptions: The system supports the specific Unicode characters used in the test.

steps.action: Submit the 15-character Unicode password for validation.
steps.expected: The password is accepted as it meets the minimum length requirement of 15 characters.

test_cases.title: Password length validation with mixed ASCII and Unicode characters
test_cases.preconditions: A company representative account is in a state where a password can be set. The candidate password consists of 10 ASCII characters and 5 Unicode characters, totaling 15 code points, and is not on the blocklist.

steps.action: Submit the mixed 15-character password for validation.

steps.expected: The password is rejected because it is shorter than the minimum required length of 15 characters.

test_cases.title: Password hint field is not available during activation
test_cases.preconditions: A new company representative is in the account activation flow.

test_cases.title: Password hint is not accessible on the public sign-in page
test_cases.preconditions: A company representative account exists with a password set. The user is not authenticated.

test_cases.title: Password selection flow does not include security questions
test_cases.preconditions: A company representative account is in the password creation or reset state where a new password must be set.

steps.action: Enter a valid password that meets length and blocklist requirements and submit the form.
steps.expected: The password is accepted without requiring answers to any security questions.

test_cases.title: Verification of a long password without truncation
test_cases.preconditions: An active company representative account with a known password of at least 64 characters that is not on the blocklist.

test_cases.title: Blocklisted password rejection during establishment
test_cases.preconditions: A new company representative account is being created (activation step). The blocklist contains a known compromised password of at least 15 characters.

test_cases.title: Acceptance of strong password not on blocklist

test_cases.title: Entire password matches a blocklisted entry

steps.expected: The system accepts the password, as the full string is not in the blocklist.

test_cases.title: Rejection of blocklisted password with reason
